text.p: Sano Corp on Monday said it amended its generic-product distribution agreement with Pharmaceutical Resources Inc.
Under the amendment, Sano reacquired U.S. and foreign rights to generic patch products that are either under development or developed in the future by Sano, it said.

In addition, Pharmaceutical Resources retains only U.S. distribution rights of Sano's generic nicotine and two generic nitroglycerin patches, which are pending approval at the Food and Drug Administration, Sano said.

As part of the amendment, Sano agreed to return $3.9 million, which represents a portion paid by Pharmaceutical Resources for certain development and clinical expenses. It also agreed to allow Pharmaceutical Resources to recover an additional $1.5 million out of gross profit from sales of products.

"We have an extensive generic-product pipeline which we are developing as part of our strategy to achieve near-term product commercialization," Sano President Reginald Hardy said in a statement. "We are immediately commencing discussions on collaborations with other companies for distribution of those products we have reacquired."
In relation to the generic nicotine and two nitroglycerin patches, Sano has regained all foreign rights from Pharmaceutical Resources, except for in Israel, it said.
